categories.description: Long lasting absence of precipitation affecting agriculture and livestock, and the overall availability of food and water.
categories.title: Drought

categories.description: Related to dust storms, air pollution and other non-volcanic aerosols. Volcano-related plumes shall be included with the originating eruption event.
categories.title: Dust and Haze

categories.description: Related to all manner of shaking and displacement. Certain aftermath of earthquakes may also be found under landslides and floods.
categories.title: Earthquakes

categories.description: Related to aspects of actual flooding--e.g., inundation, water extending beyond river and lake extents.
categories.title: Floods

categories.description: Related to landslides and variations thereof: mudslides, avalanche.
categories.title: Landslides

categories.description: Events that have been human-induced and are extreme in their extent.
categories.title: Manmade

categories.description: Related to all ice that resides on oceans and lakes, including sea and lake ice (permanent and seasonal) and icebergs.
categories.title: Sea and Lake Ice

categories.description: Related to the atmospheric aspect of storms (hurricanes, cyclones, tornadoes, etc.). Results of storms may be included under floods, landslides, etc.
categories.title: Severe Storms

categories.description: Related to snow events, particularly extreme/anomalous snowfall in either timing or extent/depth.
categories.title: Snow

categories.description: Related to anomalous land temperatures, either heat or cold.
categories.title: Temperature Extremes

categories.description: Related to both the physical effects of an eruption (rock, ash, lava) and the atmospheric (ash and gas plumes).
categories.title: Volcanoes

categories.description: Related to events that alter the appearance of water: phytoplankton, red tide, algae, sediment, whiting, etc.
categories.title: Water Color

categories.description: Wildland fires includes all nature of fire, in forest and plains, as well as those that spread to become urban and industrial fire events. Fires may be naturally caused or manmade.
categories.title: Wildfires

description: List of all the available event categories in the EONET system
title: EONET Event Categories
